name: mds
summary: the pools placed by Nei's minimum distance, on a classical MDS (principal coordinates analysis)
gates: THE DISTANCE IS NEI'S MINIMUM DISTANCE, (J_A + J_B) / 2 - J_AB, corrected for the sampling in each pool and averaged over sites. J is the probability that two chromosomes drawn from one pool carry the same allele; the sum runs over EVERY allele of a site including the reference, so a triallelic site contributes three terms and no allele is privileged.

IT IS NOT FLOORED AT ZERO AND SMALL NEGATIVE DISTANCES ARE CORRECT. The correction subtracts each pool's own sampling noise, so two pools drawn from one population estimate a true distance of zero and land either side of it. A negative entry in distance.tsv means the pools are indistinguishable at this depth, not that something failed.

The correction is what keeps DEPTH out of the picture. Uncorrected, two shallow pools drawn from one population come out further apart than two deep ones and the first axis is depth rather than biology; the raw column beside each distance is the uncorrected sum, so how much was removed is readable rather than assumed.

Every pair is averaged over ITS OWN sites, and distance.tsv reports that count per pair. A pool with no reads at a site drops it for that pool's pairs and leaves the others intact, so two distances in one run can rest on different numbers of sites.

A site where a pool has one read is dropped for that pool's pairs. Effective sample size is exactly 1 at depth 1 whatever the pool holds, and one gene copy carries no within-pool diversity for the correction to work from.

THE ORDINATION PLACES POOLS, NOT UNITS. Two pools of one biological unit landing apart is what an ordination is read to see, so nothing is collapsed first; mds.tsv carries each pool's unit so a reader can tell which points should have coincided.

Classical scaling assumes the distances fit a flat space and these need not. Negative eigenvalues are published in full rather than dropped, and every share is reported against both denominators in use - the signed sum, which can put two axes above 100%, and the sum of absolute values, which cannot. The plot's axis labels use the second.
An axis has a direction and not a sign, so each is turned to make its largest coordinate positive. Without that the same data plots mirrored on two machines and reads as though it changed.

AT SIX POOLS AN ORDINATION IS SIX POINTS AND WILL ALWAYS SHOW STRUCTURE. Nothing here says whether the arrangement is more than sampling noise; a block bootstrap over linkage blocks with Procrustes alignment is what would give a confidence region and it is not in this release.

Computed from the DEPTH table alone. Every published frequency is a six-significant-digit rendering of a ratio the depth table holds exactly, and a cell with no reads is published there as 0 rather than as missing.
Read over the SNP tables alone unless analysis.modules.mds.includeIndels says otherwise, matching how every other module in this frame counts indels apart.

A spanning-deletion allele reaching the SNP table as a * or an X is one allele of that site like any other: it carries reads, so it carries frequency, and dropping it would renormalize the site to something no pool was sequenced at.

Pool sizes and ploidy come from the project's metadata as the frame resolved them, not from anything this module infers. Ploidy enters once, through n_chrom = ploidy * poolSize inside n_eff, so nothing here is limited to diploids. A pool of one chromosome is refused: the correction has nothing to divide by at any site.

bin/cap_depth.awk keeps reads in coordinate order until the cap rather than subsampling, so at a capped position the retained reads are biased toward those mapping earliest. That is an allele-frequency bias and not only a depth truncation.

filterFalsePositives.sh admits an allele that clears half of one chromosome's frequency in a fraction of the samples, and MajorAlleleToRef.py re-polarizes on cohort totals. Both depend on which pools were in the run, so a distance from six pools is not the same quantity as one from twelve and the two are not comparable across targets.
